title: Region-aware backpressure routing: latency + capacity pinning with graceful shedding
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a composite multi-region routing policy that prioritizes latency SLO adherence while respecting per-region capacity signals and customer geo-pin preferences. The routing layer should: (1) prefer low-latency regions, (2) honor customer-configured geo-pins when capacity allows, (3) open region-level circuit breakers on sustained overload or error spikes, and (4) apply graceful load shedding/backpressure before cross-region failover when specified.
background: We currently route primarily by weighted latency and static region preferences. Several incidents (see INC-2026-02-high-rt) showed sudden regional capacity pressure causing increased tail latency and cascading cross-region failovers that violated SLOs. Product teams want a more predictable, capacity-aware steering policy that preserves locality for privacy-sensitive customers and reduces noisy failovers.
goals: 1) Reduce cross-region failovers that happen due to temporary capacity spikes. 2) Keep 99th percentile latency within configured SLOs for top-tier customers. 3) Provide deterministic behavior for geo-pinned customers while allowing controlled overflow. 4) Surface clear metrics and runbook links when circuit breakers trigger.
proposal_summary: Create a policy engine that computes a per-request region score combining: latency_score (real-time p50/p95 telemetry), capacity_score (available capacity estimate from capacity service), and geo_pin_score (binary boost/mask for pinned requests). Use tunable weights per customer class. Add region-level circuit breakers with three states (Closed, Open, Degraded). On entering Degraded, apply progressive shedding: reduce batch size, enforce stricter token limits, and optionally reject non-essential requests. Only after sustained Degraded->Open transition (configurable window) do we shift primary routing to overflow regions. Provide APIs for tenants to opt-in to strict geo pinning (never overflow) or flexible pinning (overflow allowed after N seconds).
tradeoffs:
- More signals increases routing stability but raises coupling between router and capacity estimators.
- Aggressive shedding protects SLOs but increases error rates for best-effort workloads.
- Supporting per-tenant pinning modes increases config surface and testing complexity.
- Slight increase in control-plane CPU for computing composite scores per request; mitigated by caching and localized score evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Composite region score implemented and configurable per-project with default weights documented in Confluence.
Region-level circuit breakers with metrics for state transitions (Closed/Degraded/Open) emit events to the observability pipeline.
Canary rollout to 10% traffic for non-pinned tenants shows 30% fewer cross-region failovers in synthetic overload tests compared to baseline.
Graceful shedding behavior reduces p99 latency by >=20% under sustained regional overload in chaos test.
APIs expose tenant pinning modes; doc pages updated and security reviewed for geo-sensitive customers.
implementation_steps: Design composite scoring algorithm and config schema - deliver design doc (Confluence: /docs/multi-region-composite-score).
Extend capacity service to export per-region available_slots and short-term trend (1m/5m) to routing layer.
Implement region circuit breaker state machine with exponential backoff and hysteresis; emit events to events-stream.
Add progressive shedding actions: batch-size clamp, token-limit clamp, non-critical-route rejection policy; implement as pluggable policy chain.
Create tenant config API for geo_pin_mode (STRICT | FLEXIBLE | IGNORE) and overflow_timeout.
Wire metrics: region_score, breaker_state, shed_rate, overflow_rate, cross_region_failovers. Add dashboards and alerts (grafana/dashboards/MR-routing.json).
Integration tests: synthetic load, chaos tests (local region kill), and regression tests for pinned tenants.
Canary rollout plan: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on SLO violations.
Ship runtime toggles and documentation; schedule post-launch review and runbook updates.
monitoring_and_rollout: Create dashboard panels for per-region p50/p95/p99, capacity_available, breaker_state, and shed_rate.
Add alert: if any region breaker enters Open for >30s, page oncall (SEV) and create incident link.
Canary gate: fail if canary p99 > baseline p99 + 10% for 5 consecutive minutes.
Post-rollback checks: verify no decrease in throughput for pinned tenants and validate event stream contains breaker Open events.
